cohort: The study included 722 women who were divided into three groups: nulliparous women, women who had a vaginal delivery, and women who had an elective cesarean section.
finding: There are significant differences in pelvic floor biometry between asymptomatic primiparous women and nulliparous women, as well as between women with vaginal delivery and those with elective cesarean section.
mod_finding: The vaginal delivery group had significantly greater bladder neck descent, retrovesical angles on Valsalva maneuver, urethral rotation, levator hiatus area on Valsalva maneuver, urethral inclination angle, and funneling of the proximal urethra than the cesarean section group.
